findings.breaking_input: A rendered .opencode/commands/arc-ship.md whose agent line is `agent: arc-commit-fence` while arc-commit-fence.md exists and is `mode: all` with `"*": deny`
findings.why: commandFence only verifies agent === `${command}-fence` and that the fence file exists with mode all/deny. It never verifies the fence file corresponds to this command's own tool allow-list. An attacker-controlled command can borrow a more privileged fence (e.g. one that allows `gh`, `vercel`, `git push`) and run unfenced-by-its-own-tools in the top-level session. The ADR-2027 promise (”the whole session runs inside the command's fence”) is broken when the fence agent is merely named by any command file. The fix is to bind the fence to the command's source, e.g. by checking the fence's allowed-tools against the source command, or storing a marker.
findings.fix: Require agent === `${command}-fence` AND verify `.opencode/agents/${command}-fence.md` was rendered from `.claude/commands/${command}.md` (e.g. by matching the front-matter allowed-tools, or storing the sourced stem in the agent body). Refuse NO-FENCE if the fence names a different source command.

findings.breaking_input: A run whose transcript path contains a backslash on POSIX (e.g. --transcript 'dir\x.jsonl'), which is legal in Node but illegal in the pidfile path handling/registry read; or a transcript path under a directory that is a symlink outside the ledger, so `reapStale`/`writePidfile` writes outside the ledger
findings.why: The `transcript` and `ledger` paths are resolved and joined without confinement. `reapStale` walks directories via lstat and `withFileTypes`, but `writePidfile` does not confine the transcript's parent to the ledger; and on POSIX a backslash in the transcript path is fine for node but folded to `/` by `posix()` for the pidfile name; the ledger walk may never find `<transcript>.pid`. The pidfile may be written outside the intended ledger, making the reap ineffective.
findings.fix: Confine transcript and ledger paths with a realpath containment check (as in safePath) and refuse a transcript that is not under the ledger; reject backslashes on POSIX for these paths.

findings.breaking_input: Two wrappers run concurrently; wrapper A's pidfile exists and its wrapper pid is alive; wrapper B calls reapStale. B checks `rec.wrapper !== process.pid && commandLine(rec.wrapper) === rec.wrapperCmd`, but if B's process has the same pid as A (pid reuse, or a fork that resets the wrapper pid), it skips properly; yet the main hazard is that the check only verifies wrapperCmd equality on the one hand and never verifies the recorded run is under the same ledger lineage. A committed pidfile planted with a wrapper pid of B's own process and a wrapperCmd equal to B's command line (a self-referential plant) passes the 'still running' check and is skipped forever.
findings.why: The skip condition treats 'its wrapper is still running' as 'never touch', but a planted pidfile can name B's own process as its wrapper (B is running), so the pidfile is never reaped, and B's run proceeds with a stale live orphan from a prior run spending.
findings.fix: Bind the pidfile to the specific wrapper instance (e.g. store a random token and the wrapper's start time) and only treat the run as in-progress when both the pid and the token match a live process.

findings.breaking_input: A leader that exits normally, but its group still contains a child that wrote its own command line to hide, or a child whose command line is identical to the leader; finalise kills `tree` set built from `treePids(child.pid)` while the leader is still live, then kills again; the survivors() call only checks the recorded tree on POSIX via `seenPids`, but overwrites `killTree(child)` only once, and a child can fork between the snapshot in finalise and the kill.
findings.why: The finalise path can miss a forked child because it reads the tree once from `treePids` (which on POSIX returns only the leader's group via `killTree(-pgid)`) and the pidfile's `seen` is only updated on the 3-second snapshot; a quick fork between finalise's snapshot and the kill escapes. The state then exits 0/ok leaving an orphan spending. The debt row 23 shape (a detached grandchild) is not covered on POSIX because `treePids` on POSIX returns [root] only.
findings.fix: On POSIX, snapshot the process tree via `ps --ppid` before the kill and kill each pid, then re-poll for any new pids in the group/session; refuse to end the run while the pidfile's recorded tree is not fully gone.

findings.breaking_input: A render with a path `".codex\u2215..\u2215AGENTS.md"` or `".codex/..%2FAGENTS.md"` — the check is `confineRel(path)` (plain lexical) plus `path.startsWith(root)`, and `join(tree, path)` normalizes. The tests use the literal `../` form and the probe covers that, but a path using an alternative separator (umlaut, `%2F`) or a Unicode look-alike is not rejected because `confineRel` only handles ASCII `.` and `..` segments.
findings.why: An attacker-supplied render (e.g. a malicious source-render module or a planted target) can produce a path that lexically starts with `.codex/` but normalizes to `AGENTS.md` after `join`, overwriting the brain, or writes outside the tree on Windows via `:` or a drive letter passed through `confineRel`.
findings.fix: Canonicalize the path (resolve and verify it stays under `tree` plus the three roots) and reject any path that does not strictly start with the exact root string; refuse any segment containing `:` or backslash.

findings.breaking_input: A symlink planted at `.opencode/commands/arc-resume.md` pointing to an external file, or a symlinked directory `.opencode/agents` pointing outside; the writer calls writable() which does an lstat chain walk and refuses for existing segments and the final file, but writable() returns without an error only when it does not encounter a link. However, the writer then does `mkdirSync(dirname(abs), {recursive:true})` and `writeFileSync(abs, text)`, which both follow a symlink that was planted between the writable() check and the write (TOCTOU) — especially if an attacker replaces the directory with a symlink after the check.
findings.why: TOCTOU between the lstat walk and the write lets a symlink redirect the write outside the tree even though `--check` would flag it. The whole threat model (never write through a link) is defeated by a race.
findings.fix: After mkdir, re-lstat the final file path; if it is a symlink, refuse. Or write to a unique temp name inside the tree and rename, so the rename cannot follow a link planted on the target name.

findings.breaking_input: An attacker can commit a `.jsonl.pid` file under a ledger directory with `{pid: <a current pid>, cmd: <a matching command line>}` for any pid they can predict, e.g. their own `ls` or a shell. reapStale sees `commandLine(t.pid) === t.cmd` and kills that pid. The pidfile has no cryptographic binding to the run's wrapper or to the checkout.
findings.why: The command-line equality guard is the only authenticity check; a committed pidfile can name an arbitrary alive process whose command line is known, causing an innocent process to be SIGKILLed. Debt ledger row 25 accepts clearing a pid whose command changed, but killing a pid that merely matches a known command line is still unsafe on POSIX where the pidfile was planted to match a long-running shell.
findings.fix: Bind each pidfile to the wrapper via a secret (random token stored in the pidfile and in the wrapper's environment or argv) and require it to match before any kill.

findings.breaking_input: A v2 manifest with a `files` key whose value is a symlinked file inside the project pointing outside; safePath uses realpath containment for the walk-up and refuses a symlink only when it is the probe itself. The upgrade loop then calls `sha(readFileSync(abs))` where `abs = join(dir, op.path)`; but `abs` may be a symlink (realpath outside) that was not caught because safePath refuses only when `probe === at` and it is a symlink — yet the file may be reached through a symlinked parent that is not the deepest existing element in the loop.
findings.why: safePath walks up from the full candidate path to the first existing segment; if a symlinked parent exists elsewhere in the chain, the walk may not examine that intermediate symlink because it stops at the deepest existing one (a file at the deeper path), leaving the parent unresolved. Then `readFileSync` follows the symlinked parent and reads/writes outside the project.
findings.fix: Walk every component from the project root down and require each intermediate realpath inside the project; refuse any symlink on any existing segment.

findings.breaking_input: A stale pidfile recorded a leader pid that has been reused by an unrelated long-running process whose command line coincidentally equals the recorded `cmd` (e.g. both are `node index.js`); reapStale kills that unrelated process.
findings.why: The pid-reuse guard (command line equality) is weak on POSIX where two processes can share the identical command line. The earlier debt rows accepted clearing a pid whose command changed, but the equality check itself can be satisfied by an unrelated process with the same argv.
findings.fix: Record the process start time (e.g. `/proc/<pid>/stat` field 22 or `ps -o lstart`) and require both pid and start time to match before killing.

findings.breaking_input: A generated path (e.g. `.codex/agents/evil.json`) that is hand-planted or modified with a change inconsistent with a fresh render; the diff excludes it, so the attacker never sees the planted content, and the plant could hide a backdoor in the generated file (e.g. an added permission or a malicious tool).
findings.why: The exclusion is by path, not by content-equality-to-render. Debt rows 26-27 accept this, but a hand-planted file under `.codex/` that is also a real render output (a collision) would be invisible in the diff, defeating the adversarial pass's purpose.
findings.fix: Only exclude a generated-path file when its diff is byte-identical to a fresh render of that path; otherwise include it in the diff.

findings.breaking_input: The test only asserts `arc-ship.md`'s text mentions `git ls-files --error-unmatch` and that the allowed-tools do not include `--yes`; it does not run the actual fence logic (e.g. `acceptable-tools` in the source). The test's `grep -qF 'Bash(vercel --prod), Bash(git ls-files --error-unmatch:*)'` can pass even if `vercel --prod` is allowed without the tracked-target condition — an explicit prose condition is not a fence condition.
findings.why: The fence is a grammar in OpenAI/Claude Code, not a shell condition; the test only checks string presence, so a mutant that allows `vercel --prod` unconditionally (e.g. by moving the tracked-target condition into a comment) passes.
findings.fix: The test must assert that `arc-ship.md` contains a condition statement (e.g. `&& git ls-files --error-unmatch` inside the tool call) or that `allowed-tools` always carries the `--`-style condition; failing that, refuse the fence grant entirely.

findings.breaking_input: A leader that exits becomes a zombie that Node has not reaped; the wrapper's synchronous `spawnSync`-based survivors() loop never lets Node's event loop reap, so `alive()` via `ps` sees a zombie (stat `Z`) — the new code correctly ignores zombies; but the 5-second poll still leaves the zombie un-reaped, so the process table keeps the pid, and the `.pid` file is unlinked only when left is empty. If the wrapper is run by a parent that does not `waitpid`, the zombie lingers, but survivors() will treat it as gone; the run exits 0; a later run's reapStale sees no live pid and clears. So no false KILL-INCOMPLETE, but a zombie pid is never reaped by this wrapper.
findings.why: The new code correctly treats a zombie as not alive, but it never calls `waitpid` on the child, leaving a zombie that can be recycled — yet the pidfile is removed; the debt row B6 fixed the liveness misclassification but the zombie accumulation is cosmetic (a process-table leak) and could be reused by an attacker's pidfile.
findings.fix: After survivors() returns empty, call `child.unref()` and `waitpid` (e.g. `child.on('exit')`), or spawn a reaper; treat a zombie pid as gone but still reap it.
